newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says more Kurdish refugees returned to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran says more Kurdish refugees returned to Iraq.

text.p: Iran said on Saturday about 1,500 Iraqi Kurds who were among tens of thousands who fled northern Iraq since its take-over by a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction in September have returned home.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted a Red Crescent official as saying that more refugees will cross back to north Iraq in the near future due to "cold weather and relative security established in some regions in northern Iraq."
Iran said on Monday some refugees have been returning across the border.
"Despite cold weather and shortage of fuel, the Islamic Republic of Iran is still providing humanitarian aid to some 30,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees," IRNA said.

Iran, which said in September it was sheltering about 65,000 Kurdish refugees, have warned the refugees faced bleak winter conditions at their mountainous tent camps and appealed for international help.
In late August the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), backed by Iraqi troops defeated a rival faction, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), and later took control of the whole of the Kurdish north.
Fighting erupted again last week and the PUK regained territory it lost last month.
